spec.title: PROP-065 — Structured installation: features, steps, conditions, plan, resume

status.comment: Adopted 2026-10-31 on the owner's request; implemented by the APP-STEPS campaign.

p.purpose: An installer option is an ordered list of steps a reader follows top to bottom: what is fetched, what is built or copied, which command or agent runs, under which condition, with which user-selectable features. The single-method form of `PROP-059#installer-separation` stays as the short spelling of a one-step list. The same declaration is what a planner prints before running, what a graphical editor edits, and what an agent reads to understand an installation without executing it.

p.principle: Everything is data. Steps have a closed set of kinds, conditions have a closed vocabulary, and every step can be answered "will it run, and what does it need" before a byte is downloaded. There is no expression language, no scripting of the installer itself (a script is the content of one step, never the structure), and no transaction: a failed step stops the sequence with its work kept, the index untouched, and a resume point.

p.features: `[[installer_options.features]]` rows (`id`, `name`, optional `description`, `default` boolean) are what a user selects: `--feature ID` / `--no-feature ID` on install, a multi-choice question in an attended terminal when a package declares features and none were named, the defaults unattended. Features change nothing by themselves; steps refer to them through conditions. The chosen set is recorded with the installation and reused by `update` unless named again.

p.steps: `[[installer_options.steps]]` rows run in file order. Every step has a stable `id`, a human `title`, a `kind`, an optional `description`, optional `when` / `unless` conditions, optional `needs`, an optional `phase` (`prepare`, the default, or `finish`), an optional `optional` boolean, and the fields of its kind. `installation` and `steps` are mutually exclusive in one option; `pre_install` / `post_install` keep working as a leading `prepare` shell step and a leading `finish` shell step respectively.

p.kinds: The kinds are: `sources` (fetch, verify and lay out `[[sources]]` as `PROP-059#source-build` does); `archive` (fetch, verify and extract one `zip` / `tar_gz` into `$VIBE_OUT`, with `payload_root`); `recipe` (run a package-relative script under an interpreter in `$VIBE_WORK`); `shell` (run one authored command string under an interpreter, with optional `uninstall`, `force_install`, `force_uninstall`, `update` as today); `native` (run a verified `exe` / `msi` with arguments, Windows only, with the same optional uninstall fields); `copy` (copy package-relative files or directories into `$VIBE_OUT/`); `agent` (`PROP-064`). A kind outside this list is a manifest error naming the step.

p.result: An option declares what the steps produce: `result = "owned"` (the default when any step writes `$VIBE_OUT`: the non-empty `$VIBE_OUT` is placed as the owned payload, exactly as an archive or a recipe is today) or `result = { external = "<app_root template>" }` (the steps install outside vibe and the root is registered, as a shell or native method is today). Launchers, public commands and portability are per option as before. A `finish` step runs after placement or registration with `VIBE_APP_ROOT` set and the payload as its working directory.

p.conditions: `when` and `unless` take one condition table or an array of them (`when`: all must hold; `unless`: none may hold). The vocabulary is closed: `feature = "ID"`; `command_present = "NAME"` (found on PATH); `file_present = "<template path>"`; `env_present = "NAME"`; `agent_configured = true`; `offline = true`. Every condition is evaluated at planning time from facts the planner already has; a step whose condition is false is reported `skip` with the condition that decided it. No condition reads a file's contents, runs a program or asks a question.

p.needs: `needs` names what a step requires before anything starts: `"network"`, `"command:NAME"`, `"agent"`, `"terminal"`. The planner checks them for every step that will run and refuses the whole installation up front, naming the step and the missing need; `--offline` turns a `network` need of a step without a cache hit into a refusal rather than a late failure. An `optional` step with an unmet need is skipped and reported instead.

p.templates: Step strings that name paths (`file_present`, `copy` destinations, `recipe`/`shell` text, agent prompts) use the one-pass grammar of `PROP-059#launcher-paths` extended with `$work`, `$sources`, `$out`, `$package` and `$feature:ID` (`true` / `false`); `$$` is a literal dollar. Expansion never evaluates a shell.

p.plan: `vibe app plan PACKAGE [selection flags]` resolves the option, the features and every condition and need, and prints the step list as `run` / `skip (reason)` with each step's kind, title, needs and the chosen result, without downloading or running anything (`vibe-app-plan/1` under `--json`). Install, update and project materialisation compute the same plan first and show it before the first step; `--plan-only` on `install` is the same as `plan`. A plan that admits no step producing the declared result is refused.

p.execution: Steps run one at a time in the work directory `<cache>/app-work/<key>/` with `steps.json` (`vibe-app-steps/1`) updated after each step: id, kind, outcome (`done` / `skipped` / `failed` / `delegated`), reason, started and finished times, and for shell / native steps the recorded uninstall data. Output of every child streams live; under `--json` child stdout is relayed to stderr. The work directory is deleted after success and kept after failure or delegation.

p.resume: `install` / `update` with `--resume` reopens the kept work directory of the key, verifies that the package coordinate, option and chosen features match, and continues from the first step that is not `done`; `--from-step ID` restarts at a named step instead. Without a kept work directory `--resume` is a clear error. A resume never re-fetches an input whose verified file is still in place.

p.failure: A failed step ends the sequence: nothing after it runs, no payload is placed, no root is registered, the index is untouched, and the message names the step, its kind, the work directory and `--resume`. An `optional` step that fails is recorded `failed` and the sequence continues. A failed `finish` step leaves the placed payload or registered root in place and the index written, reports the step, and `uninstall` remains available.

p.record: The index record of an installation keeps the chosen features and the step outcomes (`id`, `kind`, `outcome`), plus the uninstall data recorded by shell and native steps. `uninstall` runs the recorded uninstall commands in reverse step order before deleting an owned payload or leaving an external root; `--force` selects the forced variants as today. `vibe app steps PACKAGE` prints the declared steps and features of a package as written, for editors and agents.

p.describe: `vibe app describe PACKAGE --json` is the one document a graphical tool or an agent needs to build the whole choice: the package identity, every installer option with its platform, architecture, result, portability, launchers and public commands, the option's features with their defaults, and its steps as declared (`vibe-app-describe/1`). It resolves nothing and runs nothing; `plan` is the resolved view for one chosen option and feature set, and `install` consumes the same flags the two documents name. A feature list is flat in this version; a later `parent` field may nest it without changing the existing fields.

p.sugar: The method forms map to steps exactly: `zip` / `tar_gz` → one `archive` step; `shell` → one `shell` step with `result = { external }`; `exe` / `msi` → one `native` step with `result = { external }`; `source_build` → one `sources` step then one `recipe` step. A package may switch from `installation` to `steps` without any change in behaviour.

p.acceptance: Public Linux fixtures: a four-step owned option (`sources` → optional `agent` under `when = { feature }` → `recipe` → `copy`) with `plan` showing run / skip, an unmet `command:` need refused before download, a failing middle step keeping the work directory and `--resume` finishing without re-fetching, `--from-step`, features chosen by flag and by default, a `finish` step seeing `VIBE_APP_ROOT`, uninstall running recorded shell uninstalls in reverse; every existing method fixture unchanged through the sugar mapping. The Vim bridge and the documentation site are rewritten as step lists and installed on this host.

p.decisions: Decision: features separate from steps, conditions as data, a closed kind set, a planner, a kept work directory and a resume point. Why: MSI's features / actions / conditions and Inno's uninstall-run tables are the parts of classic installers that survived thirty years; their custom actions and condition expression strings are the parts that did not. Rejected: a transactional engine with rollback (the October prototype), an expression language for conditions (unvalidatable, unrenderable), steps that spawn steps. Revisit when a real package cannot be expressed in the closed vocabulary; add a kind or a condition then, never an escape to scripting the installer.
